Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
Welcome from the EXECutive HeadTeacher
St George’s is a one-form entry mixed school for children aged 3–11, located in the heart of Westminster, next to the historic St. George’s Cathedral. We have a proud tradition of working closely with the clergy to provide outstanding Catholic education in all aspects of school life.
Rooted in our mission: “To live and to learn together through our faith in Jesus Christ”, we empower pupils with a love of learning, excellent academic outcomes, and a spirit of generosity and freedom.
While grounded in Catholic values, we warmly welcome children from all faiths and backgrounds into our inclusive and nurturing community.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
British Values
British Values
Through our PSHE sessions, we enable students to develop their self-knowledge, self-esteem and self-confidence as well as encourage them to respect each other and each other’s opinions.
In our lessons we provoke the thinking of right and wrong, taking responsibility, how we contribute to society and being tolerant of each other and our cultural traditions. RE and PSHE are often taught through philosophy, where children can openly discuss and articulate their thoughts on various issues. We actively promote tolerance and understanding of different cultures and faiths.

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School - Catholic Life
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
Our School
Catholic Life
Catholic Life
'Jesus took a little child and set him by his side and then said to them: ‘Anyone who welcomes this little child in my name welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me, welcomes the one who sent me. For the least amongst you all, that is the one who is great.'
Luke 9:47, 48. Every pupil who enters our school is a member of God’s family.
We come together to pray each and every day. The children use recognised prayers of the Church, the Our Father, the Hail Mary and the morning offering, for example. We also invite the children to create personal prayer and provide opportunities for reflection and meditation. The liturgical year provides a framework for our worship, and we reflect each week on the message of Sunday’s Gospel reading.
We participate in the ritual and tradition of the Catholic faith and follow the 'Lighting the Path' RE Curriculum.
We are fortunate to have a priest from the Cathedral Parish, as our school chaplain. He celebrates regular school and class Masses with us each year, as well as the sacrament of reconciliation for those who have made their first confession. He also joins us on a weekly basis for the whole school assembly, where school, parents and church come together. Further, each May we have a May procession in honour of Our Lady. We also have Rosary on a weekly basis in October and May. Parents and carers are always welcome to attend these events, alongside staff and children.
The children celebrate their achievements in the Whole School Assembly each Friday morning. EYFS and Key Stage 1 celebrate Christmas through annual Nativity Plays, and we carry out the Stations of the Cross at Easter.
As a Catholic school, we are part of a wider network of Catholic Schools, across our Deanery, our Diocese and the Catholic Education Service as a whole. We work closely with the other Primary Schools in the diocese of Southwark.
The Months of Mary
In October and May, the Spiritual Life Committee lead a daily prayer of the rosary alongside the teachers. We also invite the parents before school to join us in a decade of the rosary. In May, there is a procession where the whole school proceeds around the school and then sit together in the playground to prayer a decade of the rosary and reflect on the life of Mary our Mother. pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School - Our Ethos
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
Our School
Our Ethos
Our Ethos
At St. George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School, our vision is ‘To live and to learn together through our faith in Jesus Christ.’
St. George’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School is located in the heart of London, offering a range of opportunities for children aged 3–11 to learn inside and outside the classroom. We are a multicultural school that believes in all children reaching their full potential by trying the best in all they do, in order to become enthusiastic, independent and confident learners. During their time at STGCS the children develop socially, spiritually and educationally, leaving school with the ability to take risks with their learning and learn from their mistakes. As a school, we are committed to providing a moral and spiritual environment rooted in the teaching of Christ and the Gospel values.
Our curriculum is broad and engaging for children, ensuring that all children have the opportunity to find what they truly excel at, through exploring a variety of activities. We also endeavour to instil a love of learning in school with children participating in themed days and competitions. As a school, we believe our wider community is very important in developing children outside of school, and we strive to maintain good partnerships with our parents as their input is so highly valued.
Our staff are dedicated to ensuring all children flourish and achieve their full potential. We tailor learning so that children are challenged or supported depending on their individual needs.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
Our School
St. Benedict Catholic Academy Trust
St. Benedict Catholic Academy Trust
We are delighted to announce that, as of 1st March 2025, St. George’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School has officially become part of the St. Benedict Catholic Academy Trust.
This marks an exciting new chapter in our school’s journey, building on years of strong, collaborative partnerships with other Catholic schools. The Trust was established to bring together a family of schools united by a shared commitment to delivering exceptional Catholic education.
A Shared Vision and Mission
The vision of the St. Benedict Catholic Academy Trust is to be a beacon of excellence in Catholic education. Inspired by our Trust Patron, St. Benedict, the mission is clear: to live, learn, pray, and celebrate together.
As a community of Catholic schools, we are dedicated to helping every child discover and develop their God-given talents. Rooted in Gospel values, our collective aim is to nurture compassionate, confident, and capable young people who are ready to make a positive contribution to society.
Leadership and Community
We are pleased to welcome Mr. Jonathan Ronan, CEO of the Trust, who will be a familiar face at STGCS. Mr. Ronan will be visiting our school regularly and attending key events throughout the academic year, strengthening the connection between our school and the wider Trust community.
Find Out More
To learn more about the St. Benedict Catholic Academy Trust, please visit their official website: www.sbcat.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
Our School
Welcome
Right in the heart of Westminster, just steps from the Cathedral, you’ll find St. George’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School, a lively, one-form entry school for children aged 3 to 11. We’re proud of our deep-rooted partnership with the clergy and our long-standing tradition of delivering exceptional Catholic education.
Our mission is simple, powerful, and lived every day: "To live and to learn together through our faith in Jesus Christ."
This isn’t just a motto — it’s the heartbeat of our school. It shapes a community where children thrive academically, grow spiritually, and develop a genuine love of learning, kindness, and curiosity.
While we give priority to practising Catholic families, our doors are open to all. We celebrate the rich mix of cultures, faiths, and backgrounds that make our school so special. Every child brings something unique, and we build on that to help them understand the world and their place in it.
Our curriculum is creative, ambitious, and inspiring. It’s built on high expectations and excellent teaching, and it’s enriched by a wide range of co-curricular activities that promote well-being, spark new interests, and help every child discover their strengths.
We take pastoral care seriously. From early years to Year 6, we support every child’s journey — preparing them not just for secondary school, but for life. The result? Confident, compassionate learners with strong outcomes and bright futures.
We’d love for you to explore our website and watch our school video to get a real feel for life at STGCS, a place where faith, learning, and community come together.
Mr. C Andrew Executive Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care
At St George’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School, we are committed to supporting our families by offering high‑quality wraparound care before and after the school day. Our provision ensures children have a safe, happy and engaging environment from early morning through to early evening.
Breakfast Club (run by the school)
Our Breakfast Club runs every day during term time, offering children a calm and nutritious start to their school day. The gate opens at 7:45am, with a £2.50 per child service charge (breakfast is free). Children arriving before 8:15am can enjoy cereals, toast, fruit and seasonal warm options.
After School Club (Provided by Magna Extended Schools)
From Monday 13th April 2026, our After School Club will be delivered by Magna Extended Schools, an OFSTED‑registered provider known for safe, nurturing and activity‑rich childcare across London. Magna offers sports, creative arts, games, outdoor play and SEND‑friendly provision led by qualified childcare professionals to all children from Reception to Year 6.
Bookings
Why Wraparound Care?
Wraparound care supports working families, ensures children feel settled and ready to learn, and provides enriching opportunities beyond the classroom. National guidance highlights the positive impact on attendance, behaviour and wellbeing when children can access consistent breakfast and after‑school provision.

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School - EYFS Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St George's Cathedral Catholic Primary School
EYFS Curriculum
EYFS Curriculum
At St George’s Cathedral Catholic Primary School, we embrace the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) as a vital time for building strong foundations in learning, faith, and personal development. In line with recent EYFS reforms, we have refreshed our curriculum to offer rich, engaging experiences that reflect our values and the needs of our children.
Guided by our school motto, “To live and learn through our faith in Jesus Christ,” we nurture kindness, compassion, and respect from the very start. Our RE sessions help children explore faith and develop a deep understanding of themselves and others.
We believe that early childhood should be filled with meaningful learning opportunities. Our curriculum is carefully planned to reflect children’s interests, celebrate diversity, and build essential knowledge and skills. Themes are enriched with high-quality cultural texts and linked to learning across the school, ensuring continuity and progression.
Learning in EYFS is a balance of child-initiated exploration and adult-guided activities. Through structured play, daily phonics, maths, and book-based English sessions, children develop communication, storytelling, and problem-solving skills in a joyful and supportive environment.
Warm, trusting relationships between staff and children are at the heart of our setting. We aim to ensure every child feels happy, secure, and ready to thrive—both now and in the years ahead.
